hand free to use a weapon. With a Husbandry

mount with her knees, allowing her to keep both

from the combat. If the mount is the character’s

passes this Challenge.

Union Dues: Some miners are members of the Miners

better trained and have better equipment, and they are
considered to be (Peon 4) rather than (Peon 3).
(1) Mining Tools (Heavy Melee)
AV: 4 (7) ====== Rg: y2 ====== Resist: Df
Target suffers 2/3/5 damage.
We've made a short stop in a minor Contract Town to
refresh our supplies and make certain that we are still on
course. The town is so small that it has a number instead
of a name, but with a few persuasive words from yours
truly, we were allowed to sleep on some spare cots in the
Union barracks.
The miners here are typical of those you see all across
the North and throughout Malifaux. Gruff, surly, and
stubborn are all words that come to mind, but once Mr.
McEwan had passed around his flask and Mr. Wright
had lost a small amount of scrip in a poker game, they
warmed up to us.
I admit to being somewhat surprised at seeing some
women among their number. The image that comes to
mind when one thinks of a miner is that of a somber
and hard-working man, but about a third of the dozen
workers we spent the evening with were of the fairer sex.
Chapter 8: C

Internal Storage: This character can comfortably

BELLHOP PORTER
These rotund constructs can often be seen wandering the 
Society halls, following whoever they’ve been assigned 
to. Distinguished members may have the Porters carry 
luggage as they move in for an extended stay. Explorers 
stuff the well-dressed helpers with items for every pos-sible eventuality, and others carefully hold experiments, 
ingredients, and volumes for scientists pursuing their ec-centric work. The Porters do it all without complaint. As 
such, they’re integral to the Society’s smooth functioning. 
Unusually, members tend to take a shine to the Porters. It’s 
not uncommon for the constructs to be treated like an-other member of the team, given clothing, and even little 
brass nametags. 
WEIGHTED NET
Used by hunters the world over, nets remain a tried-and-true way of trapping prey. Non-predators can be restrained 
with conventional models, but predators tear through these 
weak fibers without a problem. Weighted nets are woven 
with thicker ropes and given extra heft through stone or 
metal weights on their edges. This not only makes escape 
more difficult, but helps hunters more accurately throw 
the 10ft large nets. 
After resolving an attack with this weapon, the wielder 
may decide to spread the net. If she does, any character 
other than her that suffers damage must pass an Opposed 
Might duel at the start of her turn, resolved against the 
wielder. On a failure, the target is considered Paralyzed
(though she may still resolve her Might duel at the start 
of her turn). On a Margin of Success, the net is destroyed. 
Should the wielder decide to re-arm herself with the net 
to resolve a new attack, all targets who gained Paralyzed
from the net immediately lose it.
This weapon can also be used in canister form with the 
Netgun; in these cases, it has the Special Ammo (Netgun) 
special rule.
BOTANY SAW
Gentleman gardeners, and persons who take up the hob-by more casually, love a good bit of pruning. Botany saws 
are thin blades often concealed inside canes. When an 
errant branch or unruly twig is spotted, the saw can be 
quickly drawn and its sharp teeth used to cut the offend-ing flora away. As expected, enterprising Society mem-bers have found the saws to be life-saving sidearms in the 
greenhouses.
This weapon gains + to its damage flip when resolving 
attacks against targets with the Plant Characteristic.

MEMBER OF THE SOCIETY
Location: Everywhere…
Notes: I rarely meet many of their kind. Fleeting they are, 
simple pieces in a machine like the one she loved so much. 
Membership in this club rises and falls more often than you 
might expect. New ones believe the world is at their fingertips, 
that applying their human knowledge will decode any 
mystery. A small percentage are notable. Insightful, even. 
They understand how small they are compared to the grand 
schema. The rest of them? Lackeys. Idiots dreaming of a future 
they will never see, blinded by arrogance. I do enjoy hearing 
about their falls.
There are lots of different kinds of people in the Explorer’s 
Society! This profile is meant to help Fatemasters 
quickly and easily generate characters who can assist 
Fated in adventures and missions they might otherwise 
have trouble in. For example, groups lacking a magical 
presence might bring on an Astronomer or Botanist, 
while those who struggle with History Challenges 
would benefit from a Tomb Raider. Remember, this 
profile is intended as a guideline; feel free to mix, 
match, add, and subtract whatever you like to create 
Fatemaster Characters that are unique and special. 
Societal Benefits (1): This character is a member of the 
Explorer’s Society, and gains 1 Benefit per month (pg. 66). 
Area of My Expertise: Members of the Society must pick 
one of the following fields and receive all listed bonuses. 
They count the value of any Skills listed there as 3, and may 
include 1 suit of their choice in those final duel totals.
• Astronomer: Gain 2 Enchanting or Prestidigitation 
Magia and 2 Immuto and Distracting Presence (Enemy 
characters within a5 ignore any suits associated with 
their Skills and cannot take the Defensive Stance or 
Focus Actions.).
Skills: Mathematics, Enchanting or Prestidigitation, 
Scrutiny.
• Botanist: Gain 2 Sorcery Magia, the Natural Elemental 
Immuto, and the following Action: 
(1) Healing Poultice: One Living character within 1 yard 
heals 2 damage and reduces the value of their Poison
Condition by 2. This Action may be taken 3 times per day.”
Skills: Culinary, Homesteading, Wilderness, Doctor.
• Cartographer: Gain 2 Maps at the Topographical 
rank, 1 Map at the Here Be Monsters rank (pg. 92), and 
Unimpeded (This character ignores penalties for terrain 
when taking Movement Actions.)
Skills: Mathematics, History, Art, Homesteading, 
Printing, Wilderness.
• Driver: Gain a Land License with 20 Driver Points and 
Disguised (This character may not be the target of the 
Charge Action.). 
Skills: Mathematics, Engineering, Evade
• Explorer: Gain no more than 5 scrip of items, the 
Well-Weathered Talent (pg. 90) and Unimpeded (This 
character ignores penalties for terrain when taking 
Movement Actions.)
Skills: One Close Combat Skill, one Ranged Combat 
Skill, Homesteading, Wilderness, Acrobatics, Athletics, 
Stealth.
• Geologist: Gain 2 Sorcery Magia, the Earth and Stone 
Elemental Immuto, the Echoed Sight Talent (pg. 87), and 
Hard to Wound +1 (Damage flips against this character 
suffer -.). 
Skills: Mathematics, Explosives, Homesteading, 
Wilderness.
• Hunter: Gain Rank Value +2, a subordinate Peon or 
Minion Beast, Armor +1, and no more than 20 scrip 
worth of weaponry. Gain + to damage flips against 
targets with the Monstrous Characteristic.
Skills: One Close Combat Skill, one Ranged Combat 
Skill, Husbandry, Track, Wilderness, Leadership, 
Athletics.
• Scientist: Gain 3 Magia, 3 Immuto, and the Scientific 
Method Magical Theory (pg. 110). 
Skills: Mathematics, Alchemistry.
• Tomb Raider: Gain the All That Glitters Talent (pg. 93), 
up to 10 scrip of items, and Hard to Kill (This character 
may choose to ignore one Critical Effect per Dramatic 
Time.). 
• Skills: History, one Close Combat Skill, one Ranged 
Combat Skill, Barter, Intimidate, Acrobatics, Stealth.

NOCTURNE
Location: Realm of Shadows
Notes: Sentient pieces of broken shades. They are the first 
and last part of the realm’s life cycle: small and weak fragments 
that can only bind themselves to beings equally as fragile. 
Animals are suitable hosts. Nocturnes emerge from and take 
these forms to better engage with reality, for they are but 
listless shade-stuff without a figure. They are prey to the place’s 
greater umbral beasts and predator to all others. Light is the 
only true protection. The moment one trespasses into gloom, 
Nocturnes strike with vicious claws and teeth. Little defends 
against the immaterial. I see tiny dark-thoughts emerge at the 
moment of the kill. To discount a Nocturne because of size is 
the ideology of the idiotic.

Location: Realm of Shadows
Notes: Humans cannot help but meddle. Admirable, though 
ends in downfall just as frequently as success. A secret sect 
created technology very recently designed to harness light. 
Their theory: cages of light can fully control shadows called 
forth from that place. An idea I might have had myself before 
these circumstances, true, but I have seen the diagrams. 
Implementation is poor, especially against Brocken Spectres. 
Their hatred for light runs deep. How long will humans order 
around these unwilling slaves before they realize the faults in 
their designs? How much mercy will Spectres show captors who 
bound them in tortuous light? Little, I hope.

LAMPLIGHTER
Location: Throughout Malifaux; sites where the abnormal 
gather
Notes: Curious little beings. A line of creatures I admire. 
Guides and travelers, as equally interested in keeping others 
safe as they are treading parts unknown. They were always 
with us, I think. Flames from their lanterns keep away 
things born in the foul parts of any world; does this imply 
a connection between all darkness, if no malevolent or 
unnatural force can withstand being in their light? A question 
I will muse on while the Society tries to figure out what the 
Lamplighters are. She has asked many times, and each time I 
give her part of the truth. They have betrayed no one, so I shall 
not give up their secrets.

MOORWRAITH
Location: Throughout Malifaux; sites of unexpected death
Notes: Meeting her was a surprise, and I have not had one 
of those in a time I can remember. The other woman asked 
me to learn about the curse afflicting this one who stank of 
death and smelled of beautiful life. I learned nothing of value, 
nor shared any. She claimed vitality weighed her down. 
Nothing around her was dead or alive, merely suspended in 
a space where not even the Grave Spirit can claim them. She 
recounted souls at peace, but not at rest, occasionally rising 
and possessing nearby material so they might continue 
living. Moorwraiths, she named them. A fitting 
descriptor, if obvious. I will check my records. 
This is not the first time I have heard of such 
phenomena in Malifaux…

This character may discard a card to become invisible

character cannot be seen, and anyone attempting to

that action. Any attempts to detect this character by 
visual means fail completely, but this character still 
makes sound, displaces air, leaves footprints, etc.

-/- to any Notice duels).
STRIPED SKULKER
Location: Oceans; natural aquifers (unverified)
Notes: The samples I have been brought disgust me. They 
knew She was experimenting in those far waters, yet did 
nothing to stop her. I am torn. Her work is simultaneously 
exquisite, grotesque, and unnatural. The “striped skulker” 
exhibits potent venom capable of creating quick and lethal 
infection. Glands to excrete this substance are found in the 
jaws and near the base of its many spines. Skin has unmatched 
chameleonic properties. Even removed from the subject, flesh 
continues to adapt and shift both color and texture to match its 
surroundings. I raised concerns over these creatures appearing 
more frequently. May she heed my warning.
THROUGH THE BREACH • ONWARD!

morphia beyond size. The “armored whelks” look to have 
taken advantage of ecosystem gaps and, in so doing, can now

any engaging in close quarters. Shell curvature means ranged 
attacks bounce off the thick primary shell. I warned slow 
movement did not mean harmless. Whelks easily crush bone 
with claw, and wade through considerable offence without 
being deterred.

amuses me! The origin of sand worms (unimaginative) 
remains shrouded. Habit of remaining underground excuses 
lack of insight for now. Typically 15-30ft long, though tunnel 
evidence indicates larger members of the species could exist.

acidic saliva churn through and stabilize dirt. Worms also

in the earth, especially when prey is concerned. This could be 
how the sheriff “controls” sand worms. Patterns in sound and 
echo are essentially a language to these creatures, and one he 
clearly knows how to speak (rudimentarily).

Malifaux’s own aquatic shamblers. Kelpies, mermaids, 
nixies; all might be deviations. Wracklings use piles of kelp 
and seaweed for defense. Passive and curious, but become 
highly aggressive when searching for meals once or twice a 
month. Wracklings send out little humming calls as they float. 
I’m told humans interpret these as songs or voices speaking 
actual words. Perhaps each species hears the noise differently? 
Anything that gets close to the water is quickly wrapped up and 
dragged underwater. Once drowned, victims are slowly eaten 
while water seeps into tissues to flavor them.

HONEYPOT CREEPER
Location: Bayou, Wildlands, occasionally Knotwoods
Notes: Quite similar to Venus flytraps of Earth. Creepers 
are incomparably more dangerous. Plants are semi-mobile, 
relying on strong root structures to carry them around. When 
the creeper finds a suitable place, it plants itself and creates 
pods. Largest always turn into mouths filled with sweet-smelling nectar and sharp teeth. If fed enough, creepers grow 
smaller pods capable of greater mobility. These are attached 
to the plant, likely controlled through a mycelium-based link. 
A honeypot creeper then becomes a small community. 
The main plant remains at the top of the hierarchy, but 
podlings serve as a surprisingly effective force.

those characters’ senses (taste, touch, smell, sight,

character considers any such target with a lower Wp

furious after finding out that assistant interacted with me. 
I have not seen him since then. Knowing her, he was probably 
not long for this world after that mistake. Still, every book 
I consult refuses to relinquish answers! My mind plucks tiny 
fragments from the passages, but… something keeps me from 
finding the truth. No words declare exactly what was inside 
that poor human. What’s more, the forces preventing record 
of information about this thing are far older than she is.

this house. What has she done?

Target suffers 2/2/3 damage.

Vagabond Shrub
Yes, dear book, I can confirm that your purpose has been made to 
research and record the human (and undead, and Gremlin… ugh) 
interactions within Malifaux. I feel obligated to assist in filling 
in these enormous holes in the record of botany, anthropology, 
and zoology Ms. Bellerose neglected to include. We shall continue 
with one of my favorites: the Vagabond Shrub, so named for its 
tendency to, for lack of a better term, migrate. While they may 
appear to be simple greenery, these bushes actually possess very 
sharp, bitey mouths and what I would consider a feisty attitude. 
If a patch of soil would cease to be a nutritious spot to settle, 
the vagabonds simply pull up and go. Wherever the wind takes 
them! It’s common in the north for several dozen to bounce along 
the tundra all at once. A curious and enjoyable sight for the unini-tiated (though foolish observers that try to get a closer look usually 
fail to realize the shrubs are, in fact, very capable of chasing their 
meals). 
In my time as a botanist, I have found vagabond shrubs thrive 
when they can supplement their soil-based diet with fresh fruits or 
meat. And exercise, of course! One must make sure to let the shrubs 
wander free range for a time so they can stretch, else they get a bit 
paunchy in the root.

Movement Actions. If this character is pushed, it suffers 3 
damage instead of moving, ignoring Armor. 
Wyrdwood Forest: This character is indistinguishable 
from a normal wyrdwood tree unless a character first 
passes a TN 12 Wilderness or Notice Challenge. If this 
character is summoned outside of a forest, any Magia 
summoning it increases its TN by +4m.

Condition: “Restrained: This character is Paralyzed
until it leaves this character’s engagement range 
for this weapon (y1).” Freeing a Restrained target 
from this character’s mouth (or killing this character) 
automatically ends this Condition. 
m m Grisly Fertilizer: After killing, this character 
immediately renders the corpse unfit for reanimation 
and heals 3 damage.
(1) Grasping Roots (Flexible)
AV: 5r (13r) Rg: z8 Resist: Df
Target suffers 2/3/4 damage or is pushed a number of yards 
equal to this character’s Might Aspect (minimum 1 yard). A 
target hit by this attack gains the following Condition until 
the end of its next turn: “In the Roots: This character 
cannot take Walk or Charge Actions and cannot be Pushed 
except by the character that applied this Condition.”
r Pull and Drag: After damaging, push the target 
towards this character a number of yards equal to this 
character’s Might Aspect (minimum 1 yard).
Carnivorous Wyrdwood
I will admit, Ms. Bellerose, you were more careful in your 
observations than I first thought. But! You have not traversed 
where the carnivorous versions of our wyrdwoods exist. You see 
these trees are not entirely plant, nor animal, but something in 
between. I’m sure one of those bird-masked black blood fools 
did some sort of magical nonsense that ended up with them 
exploding and accidentally imbuing aggression and appetite 
into the wrong subject. Trust me, it has happened before and 
continues to occur on a semi-regular basis. 
If you are aware of these trees, it is easy enough to give them a 
wide berth. Skulls and bones piled around a bloodstained trunk 
are always good first indicators. Otherwise you can look at the 
leaves, which are usually flushed a bit red if the tree has recently 
fed. If the trunk is bulging or drooling a bit, that is also a good 
sign that it is almost safe to approach; they tend to get lethargic 
after eating. But do watch the roots. I’ve seen them snatch up a 
whole wild boar from yards away without so much as a how-do-you-do and stuff it right inside the tree’s maw. 
It would do the black bloods good to plant a few saplings near 
Fortune Falls. Nothing keeps a logging camp terrified more than 
a tree that bites back. Maybe they’ll 
listen to my suggestions someday. 
I can dream.

Ancient Construct
Now, despite what it might look like, the Knotwoods have a 
surprising amount of things tangled up in those old roots of 
theirs. Tombs, vaults, machinery from back before the Tyrant 
Wars. Helped humans start building those loud, clanking metal 
monstrosities that they think pass for constructs. That Hoffman 
fellow does seem to know what he’s doing. Ramos did too, be-fore someone got the geezer sent off to prison in Vienna. But I 
couldn’t tell you the first thing about restoring one of the truly 
old ones. They’re quite valuable in the right hands, and appar-ently the Nephilim believe “I am not to be trusted”.

of curious components in there. One of the most surprising was 
a set of pumps on the back of one particular construct. The con-tents were awful smelling; when the explorers broke the seals, the 
reek of necrotic magic spilled out. Ugh. Even recalling the memory 
makes me want to… what do the humans 
call it, when they expel their stomach 
contents? Ah, vomiting, of course. It 
makes me want to do that. 
At least that revelation helped me 
understand why the black bloods 
destroy these machines whenever 
the Knotwoods decide to reveal 
some of them.

a set of pumps on the back of one particular construct. The con-tents were awful smelling; when the explorers broke the seals, the

call it, when they expel their stomach

makes me want to do that.

understand why the black bloods

some of them.

Tooth Fairy
Being the consummate professional that I am, I offered to observe 
the orphanage, despite already knowing the place was doomed. 
Not much surprised me; as I wrote earlier, there was already 
evidence of Daydreams and Alps shifting between the night-mare realm and the orphanage. Not entirely sure if one is better 
than the other, but I assume both the real world and the land 
of nightmares have their pros and cons. One thing did surprise 
me, however.
Human children losing teeth is common, I am told, and so 
the headmistress did not think anything of it. When the teeth are 
pulled out, that becomes a different story. Lo and behold, sitting 
right there on the floor of one of the rooms, was a Tooth Fairy! 
It was an endearingly chubby little thing, wings and little arms 
doing their best to keep the pudgy body upright. This one was 
nibbling on a tooth like a caterpillar would chew through a leaf. 
He has proven to be a most entertaining companion, and pre-fers my left breast pocket when we are out on assignments.

Sinister Insanity
The headmistress was lucky she met her end at the fangs of 
smaller nightmares. Being torn apart is a quick way to go, in 
my experience, and preferable to losing one’s mind over time. 
Had those children continued to develop their magic and dive 
deeper into the realm of nightmares, there’s no telling what they 
might have brought forth.
But what a terrible informer I would be if I didn’t pen down 
some information for you, Ms. Bellerose? Stronger nightmares 
need a bit more substance to pull themselves out of their world 
and into this one. The Sinister Insanities are a 
wonderful example. Just being near one is 
enough to cause vivid hallucinations, vio-lent episodes, and spontaneous shattering

slowly attract one’s atten-tion. An Insanity can cling 
onto a tiny chip in one’s 
head and split it open like 
a melon. Not many recover, 
but you can’t have been ex-pecting happily ever after 
in the face of madness 
made real.

Will o’ the Wisp
Now despite nightmares usually being made of thoughts and bits 
of magic, living beasts are just as capable of incorporating a 
bit of the nightmare realm into their physiology. The zoological 
ramifications are complex and very interesting, but I shall only 
elaborate on a few of my favorite species here. Should you wish 
to consult on these matters further, we can set up an appointment 
at your convenience. 
Now, Will o’ the Wisps are a prime example. While most 
nightmares can only dwell in Malifaux for short periods, Wisps 
use magic in a more passive sense, allowing for a potent combi-nation of hunter and magic user. A Wisp does not actively cast 
its “spells”; they are far too dim (ha!) for that. Instead, they 
channel nightmarish Prestidigitation magic through their bodies 
to produce gentle, mesmerizing glows. 
The weak willed are easily fooled by these lights and become 
food soon after. Although I will say this adaptation does seem to 
have backfired slightly. Bayou predators are especially attracted 
to the lights, and have come to associate them with being able to 
snag a quick and crunchy meal. One instance when being a bit 
thick in the head is actually a benefit!

Adze
Will o’ the Wisps share a growth pattern that is common amongst 
many Malifaux species. When a Wisp feeds on enough red blood, 
it undergoes a rapid cycle of maturation. Its wings become larger, 
its body gains more glowing pustules, and a needle-like proboscis 
pops loosely from its mouth. I call them disgusting, but human 
researchers prefer the term Adze. Each one is a respectable prac-titioner of magic, which they pull from a stronger connection to 
the realm of nightmares.
Adze are unfortunately cunning, but not intelligent. They in-struct their younger brethren on proper hunting techniques and 
often serve as the primary source of hypnotizing light to attract 
prey. When a meal wanders close, the Adze will release a burn-ing swarm of fiery motes. Usually this is enough to distract a 
victim. By the time the spell ends, there are dozens more glowing 
lights just waiting to be fed. 
A word to the wise: if you encounter an Adze, kill it quickly. 
Where there is one, there are always more nearby.

Will o’ the Wisps share a growth pattern that is common amongst 
many Malifaux species. When a Wisp feeds on enough red blood, 
it undergoes a rapid cycle of maturation. Its wings become larger, 
its body gains more glowing pustules, and a needle-like proboscis 
pops loosely from its mouth. I call them disgusting, but human 
researchers prefer the term Adze. Each one is a respectable prac-titioner of magic, which they pull from a stronger connection to 
the realm of nightmares.
Adze are unfortunately cunning, but not intelligent. They in-struct their younger brethren on proper hunting techniques and 
often serve as the primary source of hypnotizing light to attract 
prey. When a meal wanders close, the Adze will release a burn-ing swarm of fiery motes. Usually this is enough to distract a

Songster
I will give you credit Emeline; you have at least recorded some 
of the curious animated puppets and dolls that seem to have 
become a hallmark of Malifaux. I wish I could elaborate more 
on the subject here, but a particular masked individual has for-bidden me to speak about anything involving puppets, a certain 
broken puppetmaster, or the mysterious song that plays through 
Malifaux, inspiring others of a similar disposition. Yes, of those 
three things I cannot divulge any information. 
But since I brought up songs, let me tell you about my favorite 
puppet: Songsters! Performers bring out miniature versions of 
musicians to accompany their sideshows. How endearing! The 
puppets try their best to strum and tap along to a beat. Most 
have little masks and colorful harlequin outfits as well. No one 
can say these Songsters don’t work for their scrip!
I always find it hard to believe that such cute faces can have 
the potential for so much violence. It all depends on who holds 
the strings.

Red Cap
Puppets are taught aggression, or they learn to hate who their 
controller hates over time. Can’t say exactly why, but the weird 
song they all claim to hear probably has something to do with 
it. There are some dolls that are just evil, with nothing more to 
it than that. The Red Caps are the ones that come to mind first. 
Little stuffed things teetering around on wooden legs. You’d 
probably think they looked like a child’s toy in part of a little 
show. 
The bloody scythe and drenched clothes usually send that little 
delusion right out the window. Something dark drives a Red 
Cap to do what it does. They gain power from blood. I would 
go so far as to guess that’s why they enjoy killing so much. Only 
purpose in their animated life, it seems. Kill, soak up blood, and 
sharpen the scythe.
As you can imagine it’s fairly difficult for a puppeteer to keep 
good control over a Red Cap. They’re fiercely impartial. Lots 
of idiots have tried to chastise a Red Cap and gotten their guts 
spilled all over the place for their trouble.

Stuffed Knight
The ingenuity of humans has really turned everything into a 
playground. Back in the day, nightmares kept to themselves 
or slowly mixed with native species until something new was 
born. But human children and their toys are doubly perfect for 
nightmares: an open imagination and inanimate bodies made in 
recognizable forms. The first time I saw one of the little Stuffed 
Knights I almost laughed out loud. How ridiculous, I thought 
to myself, that a nightmare would reduce itself to prance around 
in such a weak body!
I realized the truth a little bit too late. We all did, really. 
Humans, you see, have created an opportunity for much weaker 
nightmares to come forth. More primal things, halves of wholes, 
if that makes any sense. They’re confused and angry and moti-vated by something I doubt even I truly understand.
Keep playing with your toys, humans. We will see who’s 
laughing when the real nightmares come out to play.

(1) Terrorize
All enemy Living characters within a3 and line of sight 
must pass a TN 12 Horror Duel. If they fail, they must 
Push a number of yards equal to their Walk directly away 
from this character. 
Teddy
I know you’d think my kind would be the darkest and most terri-fying things in Malifaux. It’s an accolade I would most humbly 
accept, but unfortunately it is far from accurate. It’s too long a 
tale for these remaining pages, Ms. Bellerose, but let me just say 
that nightmares can infest more than you think. 
The Teddies that show up from time to time are extremely 
difficult, if nigh impossible, to control. You see, they are mocker-ies of goodness and logic, as, to some degree, all nightmares are. 
We don’t know exactly why Teddies are created, but they have 
shown up far more frequently now that humanity has occupied 
Malifaux. I will say that, for the most part, the problem you 
made almost exclusively hurts you. Teddies still make my skins 
crawl.
They don’t seem to be wholly within this reality when they 
hunt. It’s almost like they forget what’s happening when they 
‘play’ with their friends. Crushing bones and swallowing whole 
limbs without ever breaking those wretched fanged grins. But 
there’s something else sewn into their stuffing. I haven’t been able 
to quite figure out what, but it’s something very old, very hungry, 
and very disturbed.

(1) Brutal Blade (Melee)
AV: 4 (9) Rg: y1 Resist: Df
Target suffers 2/3/3 damage.
r Savagery: After damaging, the target suffers a 
Moderate Critical Effect.
c With the Pack: After damaging, take this action again. 
Increase its AV by +2 for every friendly model with 
this Trigger within 2 yards of the target.
m Throw to the Ground: After damaging, the target 
becomes Prone.
Bultungin
Ever since that old hole in the ground opened back up again, 
the western part of the Badlands has been regenerating. Trees, 
flowers, all sorts of old dead things plucking themselves out of the 
dirt only to kneel at the Queen’s throne. Ironic, I think. And If I 
know human nature (and I do), there will be groups that set out 
to try and claim some bounty or make money off whatever extinct 
plants and animals have suddenly popped back into Malifaux. 
Might be worth a trip back there to see if any of my old favorites 
are walking around again. I’d invite you along as a professional 
courtesy, Emeline, but the Fae have a… complicated relationship 
with the undead. 
Even if we were to venture out, it would be a frustrating 
experience. The Fae don’t travel much and protect what they 
consider theirs, even against the curious and harmless. I’d par-ticularly avoid those hyena-men that devote themselves to the 
Autumn Court with something of an unsettling fervor. They were 
all killed once and scattered like potpourri around Nythera, and 
now they’re back. Seems nothing in Malifaux stays dead if at 
least one or two people want it back.
Still, their barking and howling is so uncouth and very badly 
out of tune. A-sharp, boys, A-sharp!

Hard to Wound +1: Damage flips against this character 
suffer -.
Hard to Kill: This character may choose to ignore one 
Critical Effect per Dramatic Time. 
Frozen Vigor: This character is immune to Slow, 
Paralyzed, and suffers no damage from any spell with the 
Ice Elemental Immuto.
Terrifying (Living) (10): Enemy Living characters must 
pass a TN 10 Horror Duel when they end their turn 
within this character’s engagement range or target this 
character with a harmful action.
(1) Gigant Club (Heavy Melee)
AV: 6 t (12 t) Rg: y2 Resist: Df
Target suffers 3/4/5 damage.
c Gigant Strength: After succeeding, push the target 
a number of yards equal to this character’s Might 
directly away from this character. If this push is 
interrupted, the target immediately stops, is knocked 
Prone, and suffers 1/2/3 damage. If the object that 
interrupted this push was another character, that 
character is also knocked Prone and suffers 1/2/3 
damage.
t Chill: After succeeding, the target gains Slow.
(2) Throw Boulder (Thrown Weapons)
AV: 3 (9) Rg: z6 Resist: Df
Target suffers 3/4/5 damage. All targets hit must take a 
TN 12 Evade Challenge or become Prone. After this 
attack is made, place a Height 2 boulder that provides 
Hard Cover anywhere within 1 yard of the target.
m Bouncing Boulder: Increase the damage to 3/4b/5b.
Gigant
The winters in Malifaux can be harsh, especially since you all 
decided it would be just peachy to let a Tyrant loose. Can’t say 
I have too much sympathy, though I will give accolades to that 
pale woman keeping Him under control. I don’t think she’s fully 
aware of the competition she has in the Far Peaks. Nobody went 
up there for generations, and we almost forgot that the Gigants 
existed.
Brutish, towering creatures, all solemn and angry. They are 
all still Fae, and stronger than the Autumn Court’s soldiers. Not 
many can take a boulder to the face and stand back up, eh? Even 
though they have been absent for a long time, the Gigants are 
finally starting to descend from their caves and passes. The tribes 
do seem to have maintained a bit of their panache and culture, 
chilly as it is. Tribal markings etched on each individual denote 
status, hierarchy, and accomplishments. 
I do sympathize with your situation, Ms. Bellerose, what with 
being forced to avoid certain companies for fear of having your true 
identity revealed. The same happens with the Gigants and me. 
They are too large to imitate, and so I must watch from afar.

(2) Ice Pillar (Sorcery/Tenacity)
AV: 8 t (15 t) TN: 15 t Rg: 6

(0) Runes of Frost
Apply one the following effects to a target within 6 yards. 
If they are within 2 yards of an Ice Pillar, this character 
may select two of these effects (the same effect may be 
chosen twice):
• Uruz: Heal 1 damage.
• Hagalaz: Deal 1 damage.
• Jera: Target gains Armor +1 for one round.
• Fehu: Target gains Slow.
Cyclops
A subspecies of Gigant has taken quite well to the cold and even 
managed to change their bodies to better harness the wintery 
mountain air. They are the Cyclopes, and look just how you 
would imagine.
Each only has one eye, which I imagine looks quite funny (do 
they blink or wink?). Thick fat protects them from the cold, but I 
believe that may be a result of them simply gorging themselves on 
friends and family. The Cyclopes have runes shimmering beneath 
their skin; this is either the source of their magic or helps to amplify 
it significantly. I can’t imagine they are tattoos, as piercing their 
hide is a monumental task bet-ter suited to others of their lar-gesse. Perhaps Cyclopes are more 
like fatty balloons filled with ice 
magic?
It does raise a curious ques-tion as to the genealogical results 
of magic and environment applied 
over a period of time. Do these “tat-toos” persist from parent to child, or 
must they be implemented and taught 
anew every time, like a young student 
learning from a more practiced mage? Ah, I 
bore you! All thoughts for another time.

Lyssa
Now the Lyssas are always good for a show! Woes of rage: 
everything from a lover scorned to the relationships between 
enemies, abandoned friends, and betrayed allies. I should really 
write a book. What do you think about making me a co-author, 
Emeline? Ha! But I digress. Yes, Lyssas showing up are never a 
good sign for anyone trying for peace or understanding. I’d say 
they boil the blood, but just being near one is enough to send a 
cold shock of adrenaline through your system.
It takes a bit of time for rage to build before an individual can 
form or summon a Lyssa. I’m consistently amazed at how much 
punishment and torment humans are able to endure. But you do 
get those occasional bursts of anger, and that’s more than enough 
to draw the attention of a Lyssa or two. 
I have also heard a rumor that the Gigants encourage Lyssas 
to accompany them into conflicts. I would theorize this is a mu-tually beneficial relationship; the Gigants vent their anger and 
rage, and the Woes feed heartily on those emotions.

Lackadays
Goodness, book, how the time passes! I’ve been writing with you for 
nearly an hour, and old Lucius has yet to show his face. I would 
chastise anyone else for tardiness and laziness, but I know him better 
than that. Probably knows I’m here, if his spies are quick. They 
always are. He always picks the fast ones. Perhaps he’s taken to 
pursuing you, Ms. Bellerose? I should hope not; do I have room in 
my shelf for another journal? Who am I kidding, of course I do. 
But speaking of laziness, one of the most insidious Woes are the 
Lackadays. They drain away inspiration until there’s nothing left but 
cold and boring grayness. How can you fight against an enemy that 
cares even less about you than you do? It’s usually a matter of whoever 
wastes away first. But Lackadays always seem to be around, ashing 
their cigarettes and sighing deeply into their feathery cloaks. 
I do appreciate their style and ennui, but from an arm’s distance. 
I am a man with things to do and people to see!

Flight: This character is immune to falling damage and 
may ignore terrain or other characters when moving.
Thirst for Blood: This character gains the Fast
Condition when a Living character within 3 yards is 
killed by another friendly character. 
Mature: If this character kills a Living non-Nephilim 
character of Enforcer, Henchman, or Master rank, or a 
character with the Fated Characteristic, with a y attack, 
it may feast upon the character’s remains to become a 
Mature Nephilim. All damage and Conditions on this

(1) Talons (Pugilism)
AV: 6 m (12 m) Rg: y1 Resist: Df
Target suffers 2/4/5 damage.
r Blood Frenzy: After damaging, take this Action again 
against the same target.
m Toss Away: After damaging, push the target up to 4 
yards in any direction.
m Feed the Brood: After killing the target, push the target’s 
corpse up to 4 yards in any direction. If the corpse 
ends within the engagement range of a friendly Terror 
Tot, that Terror Tot may count as having killed the 
target for the purposes of its Grow ability.
Young Nephilim
After a tot gets enough red blood, they grow very quickly. It’s 
almost instantaneous, and believe me, growing pains are nothing 
compared to this. A Young Nephilim, as humans call this next 
stage in their development (incredibly exciting name for it, by the 
way…), is roughly 4-5 feet tall with wings and horns. Claws and 
hooves usually stay the same, but each brood can vary slightly in 
how they grow up. Some don’t have hooves or wings, and others 
exhibit stranger traits that start to become more evident with 
this growth.
As you would imagine, competition becomes even fiercer be-tween siblings and cousins. They can bully the tots while trying 
to avoid being the targets of such attention from older Nephilim. 
Youngsters all get their personalities and fighting skills honed at 
this point. Any advantage a Nephilim has is used to earn a better 
place on the social ladder. Frustration, humiliation, anger, and 
pride all mix and help to roughly form what the next generation 
of a brood might look like.
As I said, not a great basis for a healthy living environment, 
but it seems to have worked for them so far.

Now this is where things get interesting. The Young Nephilim 
eventually consume enough red blood to go through another 
change. When that happens varies on biology and lots of other 
factors ranging from magic to environment. Nephilim who are 
leaner and smaller than their Mature kin are called ‘Mutable’

location, a fluke in the maturation process, and the 
like. Mutable Nephilim that don’t undergo another 
change are likely to grow into Mature Nephilim at 
some point, but there are some broods where

Bloodwretch
Despite not being true Nephilim (I know several black bloods 
who would have my head for putting them in the same category, 
among other reasons.) Bloodwretches are the unfortunate result 
of humans trying to exploit the unique properties of black blood. 
There have been successes, of course, but most subjects become 
feral things obsessed only with feeding on as much red blood as 
possible. They will never be accepted by either culture: too mon-strous for humanity, not monstrous enough for the Neverborn.
Though it is curious: apparently there has been some relax-ation on those rules as of late. The Knotwoods have started 
accepting (even making!) groups of Half-Bloods, although the 
true Nephilim don’t see them as much more than a failure that 
can only be useful as a meat shield, and Bloodwretches are 
looked upon even less favorably. Black Blood Shamans appar-ently create them as a convenient way of gathering more magical 
power, though this inevitably ends in the Bloodwretch’s demise. 
Probably for the best. Bloodwretches are an enigma made flesh, 
for red and black blood were never meant to occupy the same body.
Well, dear book, it seems our time together is rapidly ap-proaching an end. These pages will hopefully serve you well, Ms. 
Bellerose, when it returns to your deathless embrace. Now, I must 
sign off; I believe I hear someone coming that I am well overdue 
for a meeting with.
And really, dear, trying to get the drop on old Lucius? Was it 
your first day on the job?
Love always, KN

I believe that "corpse candle" might be a more accurate 
name for the creature, given the necromancer's story. 
Evidently, the "candle" is a luminous spirit that animates 
the corpses around it, effectively serving as a crude 
hive mind for the mindless zombies. To hear the 
necromancer speak of it, such a spirit has no goals or 
motivations and sounds just as mindless as the zombies 
that it animates.
My own experience with the Resurrectionists leaves me 
less certain of this assumption. Could a "corpse candle" 
be the soul of a necromancer, its memories having 
faded away to leave only raw necromantic talent in their 
place? If so, it would certainly explain why we do not 
see more undead necromancers stalking the streets of 
Malifaux. - E.B.

Страж
Стражи были одними из первых конструктов, соз-данных для того, чтобы помочь Гильдии установить
свою власть в Малифо. Месяцы планирования, 
десятки схем и бесчисленные прототипы привели к
созданию прочной и устойчивой машины, которая
оказалась одной из самых надежных консруктов, 
пос-тупивших в массовое производство.
Основной целью создания Стража было создание
конструкта, который мог бы сражаться вместе с че-ловеческими силами Гильдии, увеличивая их силу и
одновременно защищая их от угроз. Они прекрасно
справляются с этой задачей, и большинство членов
Гильдии могут назвать случай, когда своевременное
вмешательство Стража спасло либо их жизнь, либо
жизнь их товарищей.
Длительное время разработки этих конструктов отра-жается на их поведении. Они быстры, выносливы, 
способны выполнять сложные приказы, не путаясь
в них. Это сделало их популярными среди гильдий-ских стражей, которые часто обращаются за помощью

Skills: Special
What Would You Like to Know?: For the right price, Klaus will divulge some of his secrets. The Fated can ask questions 
about anything, but Klaus usually directs his clients towards what he thinks will help them the most rather than random 
things they may want to know. He should still offer a fair amount of information on any topic the Fated ask about, but 
retrieving any knowledge that is not specifically tied to the current adventure should take a few days to receive (as Klaus 
needs to go and collect it). Typical consultations are between 25-50 scrip, but can have their costs changed based on what 
the Fated need: 
• General Consultation: Klaus offers the Fated useful facts and assistance, answering some questions and providing guidance 
where needed. No additional charge. 
• In-Depth Consultation: Klaus tells the Fated as much as he is able, and does not omit any details: +25-50 scrip. 
• Highly Restricted Information: blackmail, secrets, and other information that nobody but a Mimic could acquire: +50-100 scrip. 
• Neverborn Information: there is a premium charge for knowledge about the Neverborn: +100-150 scrip if the Fated are not 
Neverborn. 
Completing a successful Opposed Duel against Klaus will not lower the amount he charges. 
While Klaus should be helpful to the Fated, he might omit some information unless paid handsomely. This could be the 
difference between telling the Fated about the location of a locket, but failing to mention it’s also protected by a family of 
vicious Woes. Of course, if Klaus takes a liking to the Fated he may offer them little tidbits and hints free of charge. 
It should be at the Fatemaster’s discretion for what Klaus reveals. He is a man of secrets, but not every secret is for sale! 
A Pocket Full of Personalities: Klaus counts all of his non-Magical Skills as 3 and his Magical Skills as 0. He may not 
declare Skill Triggers, but gains + in all duels against characters that he has interacted with. 
Disguised: This character may not be the target of the Charge Action. Which One Is Real?: When another character 
randomizes between targets in a melee containing this character, this character may discard a card to have the attack target 
a character of its choice.

Perfect Lawn: This character counts as Height 0

of space the patch of Razor Grass takes up, roughly 2

Razor Grass
Why, she was in such a rush that she left you behind, dear book! 
I now have a wonderful little journal filled to the brim with 
pictures and stories about this little spy’s adventures! On my first 
read-through, despite having been here and there, she was miss-ing huge quantities of information about Malifaux’s native flora 
and fauna. While I have every intention of returning you to your 
rightful owner, it would do me a disservice not to inform Ms. 
Bellerose about the darker side of Malifaux. 
Shall we begin with the razor grass? Deathly sharp, I 
think you’ll find, but quite lovely in some gardens. I myself 
have cultivated a few fields and spread seedlings throughout 
the Knotwoods. I must say there is no greater pleasure than 
watching unsuspecting fools race through what they believe to 
be plain, ordinary grass, only to find themselves cut to ribbons 
on the edges! A shame if an innocent or two stumbles onto the 
lawn, but that’s the way of things. At the very least all the bod-ies cut down (ha!) on fertilizer costs and give the razor grass a 
magnificently rich color.

Снайпер Ансацу
Когда "Десять громов" хотят уничтожить врага, не
подходя близко, они обращаются к снайперам додзё
Ансацу. Традиционно снайперы тренировались с
луком, но современность сместила акцент со стрельбы
из лука на стрельбу из винтовки, что делает их гораздо
более смертоносными, чем могли себе представить их
предки.
Все задания, которые получают снайперы Ансацу, 
проходят через мастера ассасинов, сенсея их додзё. 
Сэнсэй рассматривает каждую просьбу Ансацу, пере-давая ее снайперу, наиболее подходящему для вы-полнения задания, или, что бывает реже, возвращая
задание с отказом от его выполнения. Ансацу поль-зуются таким уважением "Десяти громов", что отказ
часто приводит к тому, что организация прибегает к
более нелетальным методам борьбы с проблемной
целью.
Чтобы не раскрывать секреты Катанаки посторонним, 
каждому снайперу перед первым заданием удаляют
язык. Ансацу общаются на языке жестов, который под
страхом смерти скрывается от посторонних — даже от
членов "Десяти громов".
этот персонаж является недружественным бойцом (либо
считает его союзником, либо просто не подозревает о его
присутствии), то после флипа инициативы (но до того,
как персонажи начнут решать свои ходы по порядку)
этот персонаж может немедленно сделать один дополни-тельный ход за каждый экземпляр этого таланта, которым 
он обладает. Если этот талант есть у нескольких персона-жей, разрешайте ход каждого из них в порядке инициативы.

Mass of Flesh: This character’s Wounds have been increased 
by +3, its Charge by +2, and its Defense by -2. 
Hard to Wound +1: Damage flips against this character suffer -.
Hard to Kill: This character may choose to ignore one Critical 
Effect per Dramatic Time. 
Frozen Vigor: This character is immune to Slow, Paralyzed, 
and suffers no damage from any spell with the Ice Elemental 
Immuto.
Terrifying (Living) (12): Enemy Living characters must pass 
a TN 12 Horror Duel when they end their turn within this

harmful action.
(1) Heavy Fists (Heavy Melee)
AV: 7 (14) Rg: y2 Resist: Df
Target suffers 4/5/6 damage.
r Crush to Pulp: After damaging, take this action again against 
the same target. It receives + to its attack and damage flips 
and may not declare Triggers.
c Gigant Strength: After succeeding, push the target a number of 
yards equal to this character’s Might directly away from this 
character. If this push is interrupted, the target immediately 
stops, is knocked Prone, and suffers 1/2/3 damage. If the object 
that interrupted this push was another character, that character 
is also knocked Prone and suffers 1/2/3 damage.
t Chill: After succeeding, the target gains Slow.
m Mouths to Feed: After damaging, if this attack rendered the 
target Unconscious, the target must immediately discard 
two cards or be killed and eaten. This character then heals 3 
damage.
(1) Shoulder Rush
Resolve a Charge against the closest eligible enemy character. 
This character receives a bonus to the final duel total of its next 
Close Combat attack equal to the number of yards it travelled 
before coming within 0 yards of the target. 
Geryon
Prolonged isolation is bound to have negative side effects. 
The Gigants and their tribes are Fae, but the trauma 
of the Tyrant Wars, the aftermath, blah blah blah. You 
understand the details, probably, so I won’t go into them 
here. My point is that even the mighty Fae are capable of 
devolution. A perfect example is what the Gigants call 
‘Geryon’. 
Just a mish-mash of gray, bloated flesh and fat. All 
melting faces stuck onto bodies with rolls of excess skin. I 
have no doubt their core is all muscle, probably surrounding one massive stomach. I doubt these handsome creatures are part of any major decision making. The very few 
I’ve seen aren’t wholly ignored by other members of their 
tribe, but I think the Geryon remind them of a shameful 
time in their collective past. 
I am surprised the Gigants have let them survive, to 
be honest. Not really the best image to have such mutated 
collages of your own people working their way down a 
mountain. But perhaps the tribes have dwindled so greatly that they cannot afford to lose any of their members, no 
matter how changed?

HYDRIC SILURID
Location: Bayou, coastline
Notes: The Bayou is a remarkable dissertation on 
evolutionary resilience. The Grave Spirit’s pollution 
forces life through varied changes. Silurids are the best 
example. Recent Bayou explorations found specialized 
versions of the lifecycle. Hydric silurids are the result 
of a clutch of eggs being exposed to significant magic.

(0) Another Mouth to Feed
If this character is not at full Wounds, it immediately gains 
another head, increasing the value of X by +1.
HYDRIC SILURID
Location: Bayou, coastline
Notes: The Bayou is a remarkable dissertation on 
evolutionary resilience. The Grave Spirit’s pollution 
forces life through varied changes. Silurids are the best 
example. Recent Bayou explorations found specialized 
versions of the lifecycle. Hydric silurids are the result 
of a clutch of eggs being exposed to significant magic. 
After birth, “gupps” quickly feed and grow into a much 
larger (and multi-headed) version of their adult form. 
Additional heads do not actually make it smarter. 
Extra jaws and eyes only enhance hunting abilities. 
She’s expressed interest in hydric’s rapid growth and 
regeneration. Let’s find a way to harness it.
THROUGH THE BREACH • ONWARD!

wish they knew what lurked in the dark. Being abducted 
to the place of shadows is an ending I hope none ever 
have the misfortune of experiencing. Bandersnatches 
hunt solitarily in this fashion. Elders weave entire webs 
of shadow-stuff thanks to advanced age. Glistening 
eyes peer across any spot without light, allowing the 
Bandersnatch to hunt for prey without leaving its nest.

lairs spun with nightsilk. The elder somehow influences 
them. Imagine a single leg emerging from nothingness, 
then another, and another, until there is nowhere left 
to run. Then, one portal linking shadows becomes a 
doorway bursting with spidery limbs. There is nothing 
to be learned from these monsters. Ignore them as 
long as you can.

embraced what they saw as inevitable. Rather than stall their 
demise, cultists welcomed it. Only after His body was killed 
did the Children seek a new idol. This would be Saracenar: 
as close a substitute to His fiery might as they could find.

weakest. I believe the Children think death through flame 
will temporarily reunite them with Him. The Tyrant passes

endure after all this time... Is there some truth to their beliefs, 
utterly consumed in madness?

Фракция рамки: Арканисты.

Обобщённая иллюстрация родственного существа: Паровой арахнид

Триггеры, ауры, сопротивления, слабости, призыв и другие особые способности мастер разрешает по описанию. Автоматические атаки охватывают только обычный числовой урон.

Ранг заменяет ранения. Обычный положительный урон уменьшает его на 1, взрыв/импульс — на полный урон; особенности бронированного роя учитываются автоматически. При ранге 0 рой распадается. Изменение размера, переменный урон атак и остальные способности разрешайте по описанию.
